correctness.rationale: Exact independent Schur-complement closure for positive diagonal plus positive rank-one matrix; conditional product probability for avoiding exceptional index; exact two trace values and their difference; greedy picks the exceptional index first; rational scaling of \(n=t^3\), \(a=t\), \(b=t^2\) proves ratio \(\sim t/2\) and every normalized correlation tends one. The distributed checker checks 9,345 finite equalities and diagnostics using exact rational Schur complements. If trace values coincide the probability statement is event-based, avoiding a false two-distinct-atom claim.

originality.rationale: Relevant papers and searchable published records were compared by statement and implication, including known broad counterexamples with zero cross-block correlations. Novelty is restricted to the exact finite-k two-event trace law and sharp frontier on a one-defect common-factor matrix, with the strongly correlated near-equal-diagonal unbounded greedy gap. Literature inspection supports best-knowledge distinction, not a uniqueness certificate; older specialized coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: Broad greedy-worst-case results are known; the present claim cannot be marketed as the discovery that greedy can fail.
A specialized older paper may have the exact common-factor rank-k law or near-unity-correlation witness; a negative index search is not priority proof.
General rank-one Schur-complement identities may have other applications that could conceal an equivalent special case.

value.rationale: The family is a natural common-factor covariance and kernel benchmark with nontrivial exact pivot-selection distributions. The sharp crossover guides the choice between largest-diagonal and residual-random pivots. Its fully coherent high-correlation construction rules out a tempting structural protection heuristic for greedy trace error, despite near-identical diagonal entries.
